title: ACIS semantic-route eligibility and DXF polyface security crosswalk
mode: Deeper/broader primary-source research and plan update
scope: Widen the open-source 3D consumer and SAT/SAB semantic-reader route screen
Check legal/artifact eligibility for newly surfaced SAT semantic routes
Crosswalk BRL-CAD DXF POLYLINE face-index vulnerability report with the existing libdxfrw reader/writer guard and focused test owner
Refine PAR-07/S8 and PAR-06 implementation readiness without changing support claims or validation cadence

sources.observation: The reviewed material describes DXF conversion support and a legacy dxf-g profile limited to 3DFACE/3DMESH, not ACIS. The PDF cites a 2002 presentation, so this is a candidate route boundary to re-check against a pinned current source/build, not current-main capability proof.

Issue #228 reports a full dxf-g import-path heap out-of-bounds read when untrusted POLYLINE face indices exceed the completed vertex pool. PR #245 was open on the review date and proposes bounds validation and skipping the bad triangle. This remains a peer report/proposal and not a local vulnerability or semantic-support result.

sources.project: libdxfrw local polyface implementation and test owner
sources.observation: The local DXF reader validates the completed VERTEX...SEQEND pool before callback publication; the writer validates before emitting. The validator checks signed one-based indices against the actual coordinate count, and the existing generated test includes malformed positive/negative indices, INT16_MIN magnitude, transactional output refusal, ASCII/Binary readback, and following-entity preservation. The test was not executed in this research pass.

Documentation states that ezdxf recognizes a limited ACIS subset; unsupported records can become NONE_ENTITY with data loss. mesh_from_body only extracts flat polygonal faces, and vertex-derived bounds are exact only for flat polyhedra. This is not general ACIS-kernel or arbitrary opaque round-trip evidence.

The README overview advertises a broad set of formats, while the detailed matrix marks ACIS SAT/SAB read and write as not implemented. The format-specific matrix excludes this project from the current ACIS comparator denominator.

The product matrix advertises SAT import/export for single-body solids, without a reviewed claim for SAB, DWG/AcDs, or general DXF entity import. Published terms require prior written consent for benchmarks/feature comparisons and impose competitor restrictions. No artifact was downloaded or run; the route is excluded pending explicit written permission and exact artifact/profile review.

Official pages distinguish the open-source OCCT core from commercial ACIS SAT/SAB and DXF exchange components. The ACIS component maps geometry/topology to OCCT/XDE, may heal or approximate, and requires separate source-read/output-version decisions. It remains optional commercial evidence, not open-source or independent-kernel evidence against OCCT-backed consumers.

existingSubplansRefined: PAR-07/S8: keep carrier, AcDs ownership, ACIS semantics, kernel validity, and consumer acceptance as separate evidence layers
PAR-06 and existing polyface fast owner: map peer parser hardening reports to local validation before adding duplicate tests
External route ledger: require artifact/profile and license eligibility before optional comparison
assessment.planImpact: Add BRL-CAD as a possible explicit-facet consumer only after current revision/profile qualification; map its polyface-index peer security report to the existing guarded local fast test; exclude NativeCAD until written comparison permission and exact profile admission; retain commercial OCCT ACIS as optional, same-kernel-family evidence only.

method.limitations: BRL-CAD capability documentation reviewed here is partly historical and must be rechecked against a pinned current route before use. GitHub peer issue/PR text is not a local reproduction. Product capability and license pages are vendor statements. The peer-source screen is not exhaustive and does not prove no other open-source ACIS reader exists.
